author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Singapore Airlines plans to seek stronger governance rights and clearer loss-reduction commitments before agreeing to provide additional capital to Air India, according to sources cited by Reuters.

Air India has requested about $1.5 billion in new equity. Tata Sons, the controlling shareholder, has approved roughly $1.1 billion as its proportional contribution. Singapore Airlines owns 25.1% of the carrier but has not made a final decision on joining the funding round.

The Singapore carrier wants more influence over management and board oversight as it evaluates further exposure to Air India’s turnaround. Air India recorded a $2.33 billion loss in its last fiscal year, increasing scrutiny of the capital request.

Singapore Airlines said investment decisions would be made with its own resources; state investor Temasek would not directly fund the contribution. The talks concern potential financing and conditions, not a completed transaction. Amounts, governance terms and timing could change before any agreement. No share-price claim in this report is presented as live.
dek: Sources say the 25.1% shareholder wants greater governance influence and loss-reduction commitments before providing more capital.
headline: Singapore Airlines seeks stronger terms before new Air India funding
